export const meta = {
  name: 'treams-threading-gap-audit',
  description: 'Audit how far treams-rs threading/parallelism is from "user never has to worry", verify adversarially, synthesize a roadmap',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Audit', detail: 'one auditor per dimension' },
    { title: 'Verify', detail: 'adversarial verifier per dimension, with empirical probes' },
    { title: 'Synthesize', detail: 'dedupe, prioritize, estimate effort' },
    { title: 'Critique', detail: 'completeness and accuracy critic' },
    { title: 'Revise', detail: 'final report' },
  ],
}

const SCRATCH = args.scratch
const CONTEXT = `
Repository: treams-rs (Rust core crates/treams-core, PyO3 bindings crates/treams-py, Python package python/treams_rs, tests/ in Python, Rust tests inline). Read AGENTS.md, crates/AGENTS.md, python/AGENTS.md only as needed.

USER GOAL: make multithreading/processing across hardware "really nice, performant, and without footguns — the user should never really have to worry about it, with some manual controls if they need them." We are assessing HOW MUCH IS MISSING to reach that bar. This is an ASSESSMENT ONLY: do NOT modify, create, or delete any file inside treams-rs and do not commit. Put scratch/probe files under ${SCRATCH}/probes/<your-dimension>/.

ALREADY ESTABLISHED (do not re-derive; re-check only what your dimension depends on):
- CPU-only shared-memory parallelism. All parallel work runs on Rayon's global pool (sized by RAYON_NUM_THREADS, else std::thread::available_parallelism = all logical CPUs incl. SMT, respecting affinity/cgroups). treams-rs never builds its own pool, never calls faer::set_global_parallelism, and exposes no thread control in Rust or Python.
- faer 0.24.4 (pure Rust, rayon feature on via crates/treams-core/Cargo.toml) default global parallelism = Par::rayon(0) -> rayon::current_num_threads(). No BLAS/LAPACK/OpenMP in the stack.
- ~70 parallel sites (par_iter/into_par_iter/par_chunks_mut/rayon::join) across crates/treams-core/src/*.rs and crates/treams-py/src/{ufunc,tmatrix,lattice}.rs with ad-hoc size thresholds (64, 512, 1024, 65536, usize::MAX); some gated on rayon::current_num_threads() > 1; some use with_min_len(n/(4*threads)).
- LU worker-cap heuristic: crates/treams-core/src/linalg.rs:140-166 (lu_threads / lu_parallelism), calibrated on one Ryzen 9 9950X up to 8192 rows; documented in docs/benchmarks.md ~lines 995-1045. Dense matmul calls pass faer::get_global_parallelism() directly (interaction.rs, illumination.rs, linalg.rs ~363).
- PyO3 0.29 bindings release the GIL with py.detach(...) around native calls. NumPy ufunc inner loops in crates/treams-py/src/ufunc.rs (scalar_loop! macro ~line 565) go parallel above thresholds, collect into an owned Vec before storing, and catch_unwind panics.
- No runtime CPU feature detection or explicit SIMD in treams-rs; faer/gemm/pulp do runtime dispatch (AVX2/FMA; AVX-512 needs faer's 'nightly' feature, which is off). justfile only adds --remap-path-prefix to RUSTFLAGS. Release profile: lto="thin", codegen-units=1, overflow-checks=true.
- No GPU on main (CUDA lives on branch experimental/gpu, WASM on experimental/browser). JAX/torch adapters require CPU float64/complex128.
- CI: .github/workflows/ci.yml, ubuntu-24.04 only. Benchmarks (scripts/benchmark_cluster.py, scripts/benchmark_illumination.py) pin CPU affinity and set RAYON/OMP/MKL/OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS equally, almost always to 4. requires-python >=3.12,<3.14.

ENVIRONMENT: 4-CPU Linux container, 15 GB RAM. A release build of the extension is being installed into .venv (log: ${SCRATCH}/build.log; a final line "exit N" appears when done). Test with: cd treams-rs && uv run --no-sync python -c "import treams_rs". If the build is not done, you may wait with a bounded poll such as: timeout 900 bash -c 'until grep -q "^exit" ${SCRATCH}/build.log; do sleep 10; done'. If it failed or never finishes, do static analysis only and say probes were not run. NEVER run uv sync, uv pip, maturin, pip install, or cargo build/test using the repo's default target dir (it collides with the shared build). If a Rust probe is essential, use CARGO_TARGET_DIR=${SCRATCH}/target-<your-dimension> and keep it minimal. Another agent runs concurrently on the same 4 cores, so wall-clock timings are noisy: prefer behavioral probes (bitwise equality across RAYON_NUM_THREADS values in fresh subprocesses, hang/deadlock under a timeout, thread counts via /proc/self/status, peak RSS via resource.getrusage) over fine-grained timing; when you time, repeat and report spread. Always wrap probes that could hang in 'timeout'.

Give precise file:line evidence. Distinguish verified facts from inference. Assess against the user's bar. Where useful, compare with precedent in comparable threaded Python libraries from your knowledge (polars POLARS_MAX_THREADS + thread_pool_size() and fork warnings; HF tokenizers TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM and its fork detection; threadpoolctl's custom LibController API; numba/numexpr set_num_threads; pyarrow set_cpu_count; PyTorch set_num_threads) and flag uncertainty about those.
`

const DIMENSIONS = [
  {
    key: 'controls',
    title: 'User-facing control surface and defaults',
    focus: `Inventory every way a user can currently control parallelism (env vars, Python API, Rust API, docs) — search python/, crates/, docs/, README.md, llms.txt, docs/agents.md. Evaluate:
- Rayon's global pool is built lazily and cannot be resized; RAYON_NUM_THREADS must be set before the first parallel call, and nothing tells the user that.
- Each cdylib statically links its own rayon-core, so treams_rs plus another Rayon-based extension (polars, tokenizers, etc.) in one process get SEPARATE full-size global pools -> oversubscription; also RAYON_NUM_THREADS would affect all of them at once. Confirm reasoning about rayon-core global registry per crate copy.
- faer global parallelism is never exposed.
- No per-call or scoped control (context manager), no get/set API, no thread_info(), no threadpoolctl integration (threadpoolctl supports registering custom controllers), no treams-specific env var.
- Default uses all logical cores incl. SMT; is that a good default for dense complex128 LA and Bessel-heavy kernels? cgroup/container quota handling.
- Interplay with NumPy/SciPy BLAS, JAX/XLA and torch intra-op thread pools in the same process (combined oversubscription).
- What user-facing docs exist about threading (probably none outside benchmark docs).
Then design the minimal "nice" control surface and how to implement it given Rayon global-pool constraints (e.g. an owned rayon::ThreadPool that treams installs into every entry point and can rebuild; keeping faer's Par consistent with it; env var precedence), with effort.`,
  },
  {
    key: 'process',
    title: 'Process-model and lifecycle hazards',
    focus: `Evaluate hazards from the process model:
- fork() after the Rayon pool has started: child inherits a registry whose worker threads do not exist -> likely deadlock/hang on the first parallel call in the child. Python 3.12/3.13 on Linux default multiprocessing start method is 'fork' (3.14 changed to forkserver, but requires-python <3.14). Affected: multiprocessing.Pool, ProcessPoolExecutor, torch DataLoader workers, some joblib backends. PROBE: in a fresh subprocess, import treams_rs, run a call large enough to cross parallel thresholds (find a public API or a treams_rs.special ufunc on >= 100k elements; or a sphere-cluster T-matrix), then os.fork() and repeat the call in the child under a timeout; also with multiprocessing.get_context('fork').Pool; also the case where the parent never triggered parallel work before forking. Report exact outcomes.
- Ctrl-C/KeyboardInterrupt during long GIL-released calls: grep for check_signals; PROBE a multi-second call (large cluster or LU) and send SIGINT after ~1 s, measure time until the process reacts.
- Oversubscription when N worker processes each start an all-core pool (dask/joblib/multiprocessing): any auto-detection? (e.g. loky sets env vars for child processes; check whether treams would honor them.)
- Panics inside Rayon workers: how surfaced to Python (PanicException vs typed error) in normal bindings vs ufunc loops.
- Idle pool threads after work (spin then sleep), interpreter shutdown, subinterpreters, free-threaded CPython 3.13t (pyo3 gil_used / not declared).
Propose fixes (pthread_atfork / os.register_at_fork handling, PID check and pool rebuild, or warn-and-serialize like tokenizers) with effort.`,
  },
  {
    key: 'granularity',
    title: 'Scheduling granularity and consistency across the Rust core',
    focus: `Build a complete inventory of every parallel site in crates/treams-core/src and crates/treams-py/src: file:line, construct, size threshold (if any), whether gated on rayon::current_num_threads() > 1, with_min_len usage, whether nested inside another parallel region or calls faer with global Par inside a Rayon task. Then evaluate:
- Sites that parallelize unconditionally, even tiny inputs (scheduling overhead dominating small calls, which users make in loops).
- Inconsistent thresholds measured in element counts rather than work estimates (an element of a Bessel ufunc vs a full translation column differ by orders of magnitude).
- Nested parallelism: par inside par, faer Par::rayon(n) matmul/LU inside rayon tasks; whether LU heuristic and matmul calls are correct when invoked from within worker threads.
- Generality of the LU heuristic (single machine, <=8192 rows) and absence of a similar policy for matmul / triangular solves elsewhere.
- Whether a central policy module (single cost model, single pool handle, consistent gating) is warranted and how big that refactor is (count of sites to touch).
Use PROBES where cheap: e.g. time a tiny-input call in a loop with RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1 vs 4 in fresh subprocesses to expose per-call overhead from always-parallel paths (report spread).`,
  },
  {
    key: 'determinism',
    title: 'Determinism and thread-count invariance',
    focus: `Determine whether results depend on the number of threads or vary run to run:
- Find parallel reductions (sum/reduce/fold/try_reduce on parallel iterators — distinguish from serial iterator sums), parallel accumulation patterns, and any order-dependent collection. Rayon's adaptive splitting makes parallel float reductions non-deterministic in general.
- faer parallel matmul and LU: do the arithmetic operation orders depend on Par/thread count? (lu_threads changes thread count with problem size.)
- PROBE: write a script that, in fresh subprocesses with RAYON_NUM_THREADS in {1,2,3,4} and several repeats each, runs representative public workflows (e.g. multi-sphere cluster T-matrix and its native pullback/gradient, field evaluation at many points, a lattice sum, a large special-function ufunc array, an iterative/GMRES solve, an S-matrix operation) and compares outputs bitwise (np.array_equal) and by max relative difference. Discover the public API via python/treams_rs/__init__.py, docs/api.md, docs/agents.md, and tests/ for working examples.
- Do any tests assert thread-count invariance or run under multiple RAYON_NUM_THREADS? Do docs promise reproducibility? Impact on hypothesis/proptest replay, gradient checks, and user expectations.
Propose fixes (deterministic chunked reductions with fixed chunk boundaries independent of thread count, documented guarantees, CI matrix) with effort.`,
  },
  {
    key: 'boundary',
    title: 'Python boundary, GIL, concurrency, and framework adapters',
    focus: `Audit the Python/native boundary:
- Every #[pyfunction]/#[pymethods] in crates/treams-py/src: is heavy work (array conversion, copies, assembly, pullbacks) done while attached to the interpreter (outside py.detach)? List offenders with file:line.
- NumPy ufunc registration in crates/treams-py/src/ufunc.rs: do these loops run with the GIL released (NumPy releases it unless NPY_NEEDS_PYAPI / object dtypes)? Check registration flags. PROBE: while one Python thread runs a large treams_rs ufunc / heavy call, measure whether a second Python thread makes progress (counter increments).
- Concurrent Python threads calling treams-rs simultaneously: thread-safety of shared/static state (OnceLock, FP_CLEAR, caches), residual/pullback objects (one-use semantics, interior mutability; what if two threads pull back the same residual?). PROBE concurrency correctness with a ThreadPoolExecutor comparing results with serial ones.
- JAX adapter (python/treams_rs/jax.py and related): which callback mechanism, vmap behavior (sequential per-item callbacks?), callbacks executing on XLA threads alongside XLA's own CPU thread pool; torch adapter (python/treams_rs/torch.py): autograd threads, torch intra-op threads + Rayon; advect adapter (python/treams_rs/advect.py). Check whether jax/torch are installed in .venv (they may not be; then static analysis only).
- Batching: does the Python layer loop over items calling native per item (many small calls -> scheduling overhead) where a batched native call would parallelize better?
- Free-threaded CPython support status.
Propose fixes with effort.`,
  },
  {
    key: 'hardware',
    title: 'Hardware portability, build configuration, SIMD, and distribution',
    focus: `Evaluate how well performance and correctness carry across hardware:
- Wheel/distribution: is there any release workflow or wheel build matrix (look for .github/workflows, RELEASING docs, maturin config, docs/development.md wheel lanes, justfile wheel recipes)? Which targets (manylinux x86_64/aarch64, macOS arm64/x86_64, Windows, musllinux) are built/tested? CI is ubuntu only.
- Codegen baseline: wheels for x86-64 default to x86-64-v1 (SSE2) for treams' own kernels (Bessel, Wigner, translation coefficients, field sums). Are hot loops vectorizable/would they benefit from x86-64-v3? Options: multiversioning (pulp, multiversion crate), separate v3 wheels, runtime dispatch. faer AVX-512 off (nightly feature). Quantify cautiously; prefer reasoning plus small probes (e.g., build a Rust micro-probe with and without -C target-cpu=x86-64-v3 in a separate CARGO_TARGET_DIR only if cheap; otherwise static).
- Release profile: overflow-checks=true in hot numerical loops (cost?), lto thin, codegen-units=1, panic strategy.
- Allocator behavior under many threads: system malloc (glibc arenas) contention/fragmentation; whether many per-element Vec allocations occur in parallel hot paths; whether a global allocator (mimalloc) is worth it for a cdylib.
- Hybrid CPUs (Intel P/E cores, Apple M-series performance/efficiency cores, macOS QoS for Rayon threads), SMT effects on dense LA, NUMA on multi-socket servers, Windows >64 logical processors / processor groups, ARM (Graviton/Apple) — the LU heuristic and thresholds were calibrated on one Zen 5 box.
- Containers: available_parallelism respects cgroup v2 quotas on Linux — confirm; what about Kubernetes CPU limits / docker --cpus.
Propose concrete changes with effort.`,
  },
  {
    key: 'validation',
    title: 'Performance validation, scaling evidence, and regression infrastructure',
    focus: `Evaluate the evidence and infrastructure that would let the maintainer guarantee "performant on any hardware":
- What scaling evidence exists (1->N threads) per major workload? Inspect docs/benchmarks.md, docs/large-problems.md, docs/benchmark-comparison.md, benchmarks/ (RESUME.md, manifests), scripts/. Most runs are fixed at 4 threads; the LU probe is the only scaling study.
- CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml) and justfile 'verify': do tests ever run with RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1 or >cores? Is there any perf regression gating?
- Code-path coverage: many kernels have serial and parallel branches selected by size thresholds. Do tests exercise BOTH branches (inputs large enough to cross thresholds), with equality checks between them? Sample several thresholds (e.g. special.rs size>=64, polar.rs 512/64, ufunc 1024, tmatrix py 65_536, smatrix 512 rows) and look for tests that cross them.
- Calibration methodology for thresholds and the LU heuristic across machines (Zen, Intel, Apple M, Graviton, many-core servers).
Propose a minimal-but-sufficient validation program (thread-matrix CI, a scaling harness, threshold calibration script, perf smoke test) with effort.`,
  },
  {
    key: 'memory',
    title: 'Memory behavior and large-problem scaling under parallelism',
    focus: `Evaluate how memory use and large-problem behavior interact with parallelism:
- Temporary allocations in parallel paths: collect-then-copy (e.g. ufunc.rs parallel path collects a Vec of all outputs before storing = extra full-size buffer), Vec<Vec<...>> per-item results, per-thread/per-task scratch, faer MemBuffer scratch sizing with Par, translation_plan caches, cloned inputs per task.
- PROBE: for 2-3 representative heavy workloads, measure peak RSS (resource.getrusage(RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss in a fresh subprocess) at RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1 vs 2 vs 4 and see whether memory grows with thread count; also check memory after a large call (allocator retention).
- Thread stack size: Rayon default worker stack (check rayon-core default; recursion depth in faer recursive LU or treams recursions) — any risk of stack overflow on big problems or on platforms with smaller defaults?
- Very large problems: checked_mul overflow guards, memory-bound kernels (field evaluation) not scaling with threads, behavior near RAM limits (no graceful errors?).
Propose fixes with effort.`,
  },
]

const FINDING_ITEM = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    id: { type: 'string', description: 'short kebab-case slug unique within the dimension' },
    title: { type: 'string' },
    category: { type: 'string', enum: ['footgun', 'performance', 'control-surface', 'robustness', 'portability', 'validation', 'docs'] },
    severity: { type: 'string', enum: ['critical', 'high', 'medium', 'low'] },
    evidence: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' }, description: 'file:line plus what it shows; probe outputs' },
    failure_scenario: { type: 'string', description: 'concrete user action -> bad outcome' },
    proposed_fix: { type: 'string' },
    effort: { type: 'string', enum: ['S', 'M', 'L'], description: 'S < 1 dev-day, M 1-3 dev-days, L > 3 dev-days' },
    confidence: { type: 'string', enum: ['high', 'medium', 'low'] },
    probe: { type: 'string', description: 'how it was or could be confirmed empirically; "static" if none' },
  },
  required: ['id', 'title', 'category', 'severity', 'evidence', 'failure_scenario', 'proposed_fix', 'effort', 'confidence', 'probe'],
}

const AUDIT_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    dimension: { type: 'string' },
    state_summary: { type: 'string', description: '3-6 sentences on where this dimension stands vs the user bar' },
    strengths: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' }, description: 'what is already good, with evidence' },
    findings: { type: 'array', items: FINDING_ITEM },
    probes_run: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' }, description: 'commands run and key outputs' },
  },
  required: ['dimension', 'state_summary', 'strengths', 'findings', 'probes_run'],
}

const VERIFY_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    dimension: { type: 'string' },
    verdicts: {
      type: 'array',
      items: {
        type: 'object',
        properties: {
          id: { type: 'string' },
          verdict: { type: 'string', enum: ['confirmed', 'partially-confirmed', 'refuted', 'unverifiable'] },
          adjusted_severity: { type: 'string', enum: ['critical', 'high', 'medium', 'low', 'none'] },
          adjusted_effort: { type: 'string', enum: ['S', 'M', 'L'] },
          reasoning: { type: 'string' },
          probe_run: { type: 'string', description: 'command and key output, or "none"' },
          corrected_fix: { type: 'string', description: 'better or corrected fix, or empty' },
        },
        required: ['id', 'verdict', 'adjusted_severity', 'adjusted_effort', 'reasoning', 'probe_run', 'corrected_fix'],
      },
    },
    strengths_corrections: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
    missed: { type: 'array', items: FINDING_ITEM, description: 'important issues the auditor missed, with evidence' },
  },
  required: ['dimension', 'verdicts', 'strengths_corrections', 'missed'],
}

phase('Audit')
const verified = await pipeline(
  DIMENSIONS,
  (d) => agent(
    `${CONTEXT}\n\nYOUR DIMENSION: "${d.title}" (key: ${d.key}).\n\n${d.focus}\n\nReport the 4-14 most important findings for this dimension, prioritized, no padding. Severity is relative to the user's bar: 'critical' = a normal user can hit a hang, crash, wrong result, or order-of-magnitude slowdown without doing anything unusual; 'high' = likely to bite real users or blocks the "never worry" goal; 'medium' = noticeable rough edge; 'low' = polish. Include strengths (what is already good) so the overall assessment is calibrated. Set dimension="${d.key}".`,
    { label: `audit:${d.key}`, phase: 'Audit', schema: AUDIT_SCHEMA },
  ),
  (audit, d) => {
    if (!audit) return null
    return agent(
      `${CONTEXT}\n\nYou are an ADVERSARIAL VERIFIER for dimension "${d.title}" (key: ${d.key}). An auditor produced the findings below. For EACH finding, try hard to REFUTE it: re-read the cited code yourself, check whether existing code, docs, or tests already handle it, whether the failure scenario actually occurs, and whether severity or effort is overstated or understated. Run the empirical probe where feasible and record the exact command and output. If evidence is weak or you cannot check it, use 'unverifiable' or 'refuted' rather than giving the benefit of the doubt. Also check the auditor's strengths for accuracy, and record genuinely important issues in this dimension the auditor missed (with evidence; do not pad).\n\nAUDITOR OUTPUT (JSON):\n${JSON.stringify(audit, null, 1)}\n\nSet dimension="${d.key}".`,
      { label: `verify:${d.key}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERIFY_SCHEMA },
    ).then((v) => ({ key: d.key, title: d.title, audit, verify: v }))
  },
)

const results = verified.filter(Boolean)
const dropped = DIMENSIONS.filter((d) => !results.find((r) => r.key === d.key)).map((d) => d.key)
if (dropped.length) log(`WARNING: dimensions with no verified result: ${dropped.join(', ')}`)

// Merge each finding with its verdict; keep refuted ones out of synthesis input but count them.
const merged = results.map((r) => {
  const verdicts = (r.verify && r.verify.verdicts) || []
  const byId = Object.fromEntries(verdicts.map((v) => [v.id, v]))
  const findings = (r.audit.findings || []).map((f) => ({ ...f, verification: byId[f.id] || { verdict: 'unverified' } }))
  const kept = findings.filter((f) => f.verification.verdict !== 'refuted' && f.verification.adjusted_severity !== 'none')
  const refuted = findings.filter((f) => !kept.includes(f)).map((f) => ({ id: f.id, title: f.title, reason: f.verification.reasoning }))
  return {
    dimension: r.key,
    title: r.title,
    state_summary: r.audit.state_summary,
    strengths: r.audit.strengths,
    strengths_corrections: r.verify ? r.verify.strengths_corrections : [],
    findings: kept,
    verifier_added: r.verify ? r.verify.missed : [],
    refuted,
    probes_run: r.audit.probes_run,
  }
})
const totals = merged.reduce((a, m) => ({ kept: a.kept + m.findings.length + m.verifier_added.length, refuted: a.refuted + m.refuted.length }), { kept: 0, refuted: 0 })
log(`Verified: ${totals.kept} findings kept (incl. verifier additions), ${totals.refuted} refuted`)

phase('Synthesize')
const SYNTH_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    headline: { type: 'string', description: 'one-paragraph answer to "how much is missing?"' },
    report_markdown: { type: 'string', description: 'full report in GitHub markdown' },
    total_effort_days: { type: 'string', description: 'range in dev-days for reaching the bar' },
    roadmap: {
      type: 'array',
      items: {
        type: 'object',
        properties: {
          tier: { type: 'string', enum: ['P0-footgun', 'P1-controls-defaults', 'P2-performance-consistency', 'P3-validation-docs', 'P4-nice-to-have'] },
          title: { type: 'string' },
          source_ids: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' }, description: 'dimension:id of merged findings' },
          why: { type: 'string' },
          design: { type: 'string' },
          effort: { type: 'string', enum: ['S', 'M', 'L'] },
          depends_on: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
        },
        required: ['tier', 'title', 'source_ids', 'why', 'design', 'effort', 'depends_on'],
      },
    },
  },
  required: ['headline', 'report_markdown', 'total_effort_days', 'roadmap'],
}
const synthesis = await agent(
  `${CONTEXT}\n\nYou are the SYNTHESIZER. Below are adversarially verified audit results for 8 dimensions of treams-rs threading/parallelism (refuted findings removed but listed). Produce the answer to the user's question: "I'd like to make this really nice, performant, and without footguns — the user should never really have to worry about it (with some manual controls if they need to). How much do you think is missing for that?"\n\nRequirements:\n- Deduplicate across dimensions (the same root cause often appears in several).\n- Give a calibrated headline: what is already solid vs what is missing, and an honest total effort range in dev-days.\n- Prioritized roadmap in tiers: P0 footguns (hangs, wrong/irreproducible results, crashes), P1 controls and defaults, P2 performance consistency (central parallel policy, thresholds, nested parallelism), P3 validation and docs, P4 nice-to-have. For each item: design sketch concrete enough to implement (API names, where in code), effort, dependencies.\n- Include a concrete proposed target design for the user-facing control surface (Python API + env vars + Rust side) and the defaults it should pick, consistent with repo rules (minimal dependencies, Rust owns numerics, Python owns semantics; generated docs/catalog must come from source data).\n- Only use claims supported by the verified evidence; when something is unverified, say so. Mention probes that were actually run and their outcomes where they matter (e.g. fork hang reproduced or not).\n- report_markdown: a well-structured report (sections: Verdict; What is already good; What is missing (by tier, with evidence refs as file:line); Proposed target design; Sequenced plan with effort; Open questions / unverified). Keep it tight: no filler.\n\nVERIFIED RESULTS (JSON):\n${JSON.stringify(merged, null, 1)}`,
  { label: 'synthesize', phase: 'Synthesize', schema: SYNTH_SCHEMA },
)

phase('Critique')
const CRITIC_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    issues: {
      type: 'array',
      items: {
        type: 'object',
        properties: {
          kind: { type: 'string', enum: ['unsupported-claim', 'factual-error', 'missing-area', 'bad-priority', 'effort-misestimate', 'design-flaw', 'conflicts-repo-rules'] },
          detail: { type: 'string' },
          correction: { type: 'string' },
          evidence: { type: 'string' },
        },
        required: ['kind', 'detail', 'correction', 'evidence'],
      },
    },
    overall: { type: 'string' },
  },
  required: ['issues', 'overall'],
}
const critique = await agent(
  `${CONTEXT}\n\nYou are a COMPLETENESS AND ACCURACY CRITIC. Below is a synthesized report about how far treams-rs threading is from the user's bar, plus the verified per-dimension evidence it was built from.
